newsitem.title: USA: Dole charges Democrats with "laundering" funds.
newsitem.headline: Dole charges Democrats with "laundering" funds.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole on Thursday pledged to wage an all-out battle for vote-rich California and charged the Democrats with "money laundering" foreign money for their campaign treasury.
At rallies here and earlier in Riverside, California, Dole also attacked President Bill Clinton for a "sorry record" on illegal immigration and drugs, which are heated issues in this vital state.

Dole, behind in polls but upbeat after his final debate with Clinton on Wednesday night in San Diego, told reporters he would make an "all-out" fight for the nation's most populous state's 54 electoral votes.

And following up on his earlier aggressive attacks on Clinton's White House for alleged ethical lapses, Dole told a partisan audience here in a speech that "We're going to get tough in this campaign, you haven't seen anything yet."

He accelerated his accusations that Democrats were getting thousands of dollars in what he saw as improper contributions from foreigners, a line of attack he started by criticizing earlier donations from a couple associated with the Lippo Group banking giant in Indonesia.
He charged that "somebody brought in the cash" and somebody passed it on.
"That's called money laundering," Dole said and promised "We're going to find out how much of this has been going on -- how many countries, Mr President?

He told rallies the Democratic Party and Vice President Al Gore held a fundraiser in a Buddhist temple in California, saying that although members of the sect take vows of poverty thousands of dollars were raised.
He said Democats "are going to stonewall ... until Nov 6," the day after Election Day. Democrats have denied any improprieties in contributions.
Dole told supporters at every rally, "I'm going to fight for California -- and I will win California on Nov. 5."

The Republican candidate's campaign manager, Scott Reed, told reporters that an overnight Dole campaign tracking poll showed the former Senate majority leader closing to within 8 percentage points of Clinton in this state where Clinton held a lead in polls of over 20 points last month.
Reed said the campaign would commit whatever resources were necessary to win California, which represents almost one-fifth of the 270 electoral votes needed to win election.
He later told reporters the campaign would spend "in the millions" in television ads and would start two on Friday on truthfulness and trust with one featuring Dole's wife, Elizabeth.

Dole coupled his commitment to fight for California with accusations that Clinton has been soft on illegal immigrants, which has been a major problem in this state that pays millions of dollars in health and education benefits to immigrants.

"Bill Clinton comes to this state with sympathetic words for the people of California," said Dole. "But the problem is this -- when decision time comes, whenever he has to choose between California taxpayers and the militant groups who demand public support for illegal aliens -- he sides with the special interests."

Dole said it is the federal government's responsibility to protect its borders. "During the last four years, it has failed in that duty -- big time," said Dole. "And you are the ones who pay the price for that monumental failure."
He added, "Right alongside the administration's sorry record on illegal immigration is its dismal record on illegal drugs."
